name: Trail Pup
stageDescriptions: A round-bellied puppy with muddy paws. Too eager to be useful, but it tries.
A leggy hound who's grown into its ears. Leads you onto paths you didn't know existed.
A grey-muzzled elder with knowing eyes. It has seen every trail and remembers most.
flavor: A cast-off from a hunting lodge that took a liking to a stranger. Trail Pups imprint on the first person who keeps pace with them.

name: Pond Frog
stageDescriptions: A tadpole in a glass jar. Little more than a shadow and a tail.
A sleek froglet, jade-green, forever leaping just out of reach.
A pond-elder the size of a lunch bowl, its throat a low drum at dusk.
flavor: Pond Frogs appear where runoff collects. They travel in the pockets of walkers, demanding nothing but the occasional pause near still water.

name: Field Mouse
stageDescriptions: A pink-nosed pup no bigger than a thumb, all whiskers and trust.
A quick russet mouse that knows every seam in your coat pocket.
A wizened brown-grey creature with a coin-scratched tail. A known accomplice.
flavor: Field Mice thieve small bright things and leave them in their owners' bags. The city guard has opinions. The owner rarely does.

name: Road Sparrow
stageDescriptions: A downy chick with oversized wings. More fluff than bird.
A quick brown sparrow who flies ahead as a scout.
A weathered dusk-breasted sparrow who has flown every road you will ever take.
flavor: Road Sparrows are the couriers' pets. They appear at roadside inns and pick their own keepers by landing on boots.

name: Smoke Moth
stageDescriptions: A grey caterpillar with a faint silver trail, curled on a leaf.
A palm-sized chrysalis, ash-colored, vibrating at the edges.
A dusk-moth with wings that scatter pale smoke where they beat.
flavor: Smoke Moths are drawn to bright finds. They circle treasure with a faint glow, always the first to notice a dropped coin.

name: Forge Fox
stageDescriptions: A soot-smudged kit with bright orange paws. Sneezes sparks.
A slim red fox with blackened fur at the tips, tail like a flame.
A broad-shouldered forge fox whose every step leaves a coin-shaped glow in the grass.
flavor: Forge Foxes were the familiars of smiths before the forges went cold. They seek warm-handed travelers and the clink of metal.

name: Ember Salamander
stageDescriptions: A palm-length salamander, orange with cool black eyes.
A banded ember-lizard whose skin warms the stone it lies on.
A crimson-backed elder whose shed skin glows for hours in the dark.
flavor: Ember Salamanders live in volcanic springs and old bath-houses. They bond with athletes who train in heat.

name: Cave Bat
stageDescriptions: A thumb-sized bat pup clinging upside-down to anything warm.
A leather-winged bat of middling size, echolocating softly in the dark.
A broad-winged cave-elder whose sonar catches what eyes miss.
flavor: Cave Bats perch in the eaves of travelers' packs. They are silent except at night, when they announce hidden treasures with soft chirps.

name: Summit Goat
stageDescriptions: A kid goat, barely steady on its legs, but fearless about edges.
A short-horned goat with black stripes, climbing cliff faces effortlessly.
A silver-bearded mountain goat, horns curved like a crown, eyes pale as glacier ice.
flavor: Summit Goats follow hikers to high places. They don't come when called — they lead, and the hiker follows if they're wise.

name: Crystal Lynx
stageDescriptions: A translucent lynx kitten whose fur catches the light at odd angles.
A long-limbed juvenile lynx, coat shimmering like frost on dark stone.
A full-grown lynx whose every pawprint leaves a brief crystalline shimmer.
flavor: Crystal Lynxes emerge from frozen caves in the first thaw. They choose their keepers by sitting at a door and refusing to leave.

name: Glacier Hare
stageDescriptions: A small white leveret that trembles and darts at every shadow.
A long-eared mountain hare with pale blue-tipped fur, swift and patient.
A heavy-pawed glacier hare whose coat is a map of old storms.
flavor: Glacier Hares are said to protect travelers from the worst of cold days. Those who carry one lose fewer days to the thaw.

name: Storm Crow
stageDescriptions: A black-feathered chick with bright eyes and a loud, insistent voice.
A mid-sized corvid with a dark sheen of blue-black, watching everything.
A heavy storm-crow whose wingbeats crackle faintly before a downpour.
flavor: Storm Crows trail travelers before bad weather and lead them to shelter. They hoard bright trinkets in their nests, which they share with their bonded keeper.

name: Ridge Ram
stageDescriptions: A spring-born lamb, already too sure-footed for its own size.
A young ram with spiraling horns, dark-coated against the snow.
A weathered ridge-ram whose horns scrape the sky on the high passes.
flavor: Ridge Rams are the herald animals of mountain clans. They don't follow — they accompany. A keeper who tires first is considered weak.

name: Leviathan Calf
stageDescriptions: A palm-sized translucent whale-calf floating in a bottle of sea water.
A knee-length leviathan whose tail ripples the air around it.
A full leviathan whose eye is the size of a fist, and who has yet to be surprised by anything.
flavor: Leviathans are ancient. This one is not. It was found in a shell on a beach after a three-day storm, and has not yet learned to fear anything, least of all its keeper.

name: Phoenix Ember
stageDescriptions: A cupped coal that never cools, faintly shaped like a bird.
A fledgling phoenix the size of a cat, feathers edged in live fire.
A full phoenix whose wingbeats leave a trail of slow-falling embers.
flavor: Phoenix Embers are said to hatch from coals that have been kept burning for seven consecutive years. No keeper admits to this, and yet there they are.
